content.text: Confirmed: I have the instruction letter for the residential condition report on 14 Kirkgate, Dunmore (inspected 7 October 2026), and I will draft each section from the site notes, [withheld] words each, with no market value or valuation figures and no opinion on the asking price or whether to buy.
I'll pull the site notes for the roof first.

**Roof**

The roof is covered in slate with a rear dormer. We inspected it from ground level, from the roof void and, where access allowed, with binoculars. Access to some areas was limited by stored items, so parts of the roof could not be fully examined.

The most significant finding is that the roof void timbers are defective in several locations, and moisture readings in places were high, at up to 19 per cent. Prompt repair by a competent contractor is advised, and a contractor should also check the cause of the moisture before repairs are carried out. Several slates, lead flashings, sarking boards and felt underlay areas are also defective and need prompt attention. Other areas are in poor condition, and repair within the next year is advised. Some ridge tiles, valley gutters and flashings show wear consistent with age and can be monitored and repaired as part of routine maintenance.

Two slates have slipped over the rear dormer and should be re-fixed. The lead flashings are sound.

Please note that the site notes contain a large number of individual observations that conflict with one another; for example, the same elements are recorded as both sound and defective. Before this section is issued, please confirm the final condition of each element with the site notes.
I'll pull the site notes for the chimney and dormer.

**Chimney and dormer**

The chimney stack and the rear dormer were inspected from ground level, with binoculars, and from within the property where access allowed. Stored items limited access to parts of the stack and dormer, so some elements could not be fully checked.

The flaunching to the chimney is cracked. Since the site notes record several flaunching areas as in poor or defective condition, a contractor should carry out prompt repairs to the flaunching, with the rest of the stack monitored. Some chimney pots and lead aprons are in poor condition or defective and need repair within the next year or sooner. A number of chimney pots and stack areas show moisture readings of up to 22 per cent, which suggests water penetration, so a contractor should check these.

The dormer cheeks are sound. The dormer roof and dormer window have a mix of conditions recorded, with some areas in good condition and others defective or in poor condition. Repairs to the dormer window and roof should be prioritised, and the lead aprons should be checked.

The site notes record many conflicting observations for the same elements. Please confirm the final condition of the dormer roof, dormer window and lead aprons before this section is issued.
I'll pull the site notes for the external walls.

**External walls**

The house has rendered cavity walls. The walls were inspected from ground level and, where possible, with binoculars. Stored items restricted access to parts of the party wall line and some other areas.

The walls are in mixed condition. Hairline cracking to the front roughcast below the bay has been noted. It is not progressive, and it should be monitored, with cracks repaired as part of routine maintenance. Some areas of the render, including parts of the rear render and the gable render, are defective or in poor condition, and prompt repair by a competent contractor is advised. Other areas show only wear consistent with age and can be monitored.

Moisture readings were taken at several points, with some high readings of up to 23 per cent recorded at the base course and party wall line. These readings suggest that moisture may be entering the walls at ground level, so a contractor should investigate the cause before repairs are carried out.

The site notes contain many conflicting observations for the same elements, so the final condition of the render and the party wall line should be confirmed before this section is issued.
I'll pull the damp site notes.

**Damp**

Damp was checked using moisture readings and visual inspection at ground level, including the gable wall at skirting level, the hall floor, the under-stair cupboard, the rear kitchen wall, the bathroom ceiling, the front bedroom chimney breast and the sub-floor vents. Access to parts of the under-stair cupboard and sub-floor vents was limited by stored items.

Moisture readings of 18 to 22 per cent were recorded at the gable wall at skirting level. This indicates that damp is present and should be investigated by a specialist damp contractor before any remedial work is carried out. Elevated readings were also recorded at the hall floor, the rear kitchen wall and the front bedroom chimney breast, and several areas are recorded as defective or in poor condition, with prompt or near-term repair advised.

Given the readings, the likely source of the moisture should be identified first. This could include ground-level water entry, a blocked or inadequate damp-proof course, or lack of ventilation under the floors. Remedial work should follow once the cause is confirmed.

The site notes contain many conflicting observations for the same elements, and some readings are recorded for areas that are also described as sound. Please confirm the final condition of the gable wall, the hall floor and the sub-floor vents before this section is issued.

**Windows and doors**

The windows and doors were inspected from ground level, with binoculars where needed, and from inside the property where access allowed. Stored items limited access to some windows, the front door and the patio screen.

The rear kitchen window frame has decayed at the cill, and this should be repaired or replaced by a competent contractor. The site notes also record the rear kitchen window as defective in places, so the repair should be prioritised. The front bay windows, bedroom casements and dormer window show a mix of conditions, from good to defective, with several areas recorded as in poor condition and repair advised within the next year. Some elements are recorded as in good condition, but these need checking.

Several doors are in poor or defective condition, including the front and back doors. Prompt repair by a competent contractor is advised for the defective doors, and the others should be repaired within the next year. The patio screen is in mixed condition, with some areas defective.

Readings of up to 23 per cent were recorded at the bedroom casements and the patio screen, which may indicate moisture. Given the earlier damp findings, a contractor should check whether moisture is affecting the frames.

The site notes contain conflicting observations for the same elements, so please confirm the final condition of the front bay windows, the front door and the patio screen before this section is issued.

**Services**

The services were checked visually from ground level and, where access allowed, from within the property. The gas boiler is [withheld] years old. The consumer unit is modern. We did not see a gas safety record during the inspection.

The absence of a gas safety record is a key point for the client. A Gas Safe registered engineer should carry out a full gas safety check on the boiler and gas installation, and provide a certificate, before the property is occupied or if no recent certificate can be found. We did not test any services, so this section does not confirm that they work safely.

The site notes record the gas boiler as defective in some places and in poor condition in others. Prompt repair by a competent contractor is advised for the defective elements. The wiring is recorded as defective or in poor condition in several places, and a qualified electrician should inspect it, with repairs made where needed. The radiators and smoke alarms also show defects, and the smoke alarms should be checked and replaced where necessary. The cold water main and hot water cylinder are recorded as defective or in poor condition in places, with repairs advised.

The site notes contain conflicting observations for the same elements, so please confirm the final condition of the gas boiler, wiring and smoke alarms before this section is issued.

**Interior**

The interior was inspected visually from floor level and, where access allowed, by checking ceilings, walls, floors and the loft hatch. Stored items limited access to parts of the living room, kitchen and bedrooms, so some areas could not be fully examined.

The bathroom ceiling is stained beneath the dormer. This staining is consistent with water entering from the dormer above, so it should be investigated alongside the dormer repairs described earlier. Until the source is confirmed and repaired, the stain may recur.

Elsewhere, the stair balustrade, living room cornice, kitchen floor and bathroom tiling are recorded as defective or in poor condition in places, and prompt or near-term repair by a competent contractor is advised. Several ceilings show moisture readings of up to 22 per cent, which suggests a moisture source that should be traced. Other areas, including some ceilings, cornices and floors, show only wear consistent with age and can be monitored and maintained as part of normal upkeep.

The site notes contain conflicting observations for the same elements, so please confirm the final condition of the bathroom ceiling, stair balustrade and kitchen floor before this section is issued.

**Garden and boundaries**

The garden and boundaries were inspected from ground level, with binoculars where needed. Stored items limited access to parts of the boundaries, gate and paths, so some areas could not be fully checked.

The rear fence is leaning. It is recorded as defective in places, and prompt repair or replacement by a competent contractor is advised. Other sections of the rear fence are in poor condition, and repair within the next year is advised. The front boundary wall is sound and only needs monitoring as part of routine maintenance, although some sections are recorded as defective or in poor condition, so a contractor should confirm this.

The paths, patio and gate are in mixed condition. Several sections of path and patio are defective or in poor condition, so prompt or near-term repair is advised to reduce trip hazards. Moisture readings of up to 22 per cent were recorded in places, which may be related to the damp issues noted elsewhere.

Trees close to the house are recorded in poor or defective condition in some places. A qualified arboriculturist should inspect them, as roots and branches can affect foundations, drains and boundaries.

The site notes contain conflicting observations for the same elements, so please confirm the final condition of the rear fence and front boundary wall before this section is issued.

**Outbuildings**

The outbuildings were inspected from ground level, with binoculars where needed. Stored items limited access to the garage door, shed and greenhouse, so some areas could not be fully checked.

The detached garage roof and walls are in poor condition in places, and repair within the next year is advised. The garage roof sheets may contain asbestos. They should not be disturbed, drilled or cut. A suitably qualified contractor should be asked to test them before any work is carried out. The garage door is also in poor condition in places and needs repair or replacement.

The timber shed is in good condition in places, but other areas are defective or in poor condition, so prompt or near-term repair is advised. The shed floor shows a moisture reading of up to 23 per cent and is defective in places.

The greenhouse is defective in places and in poor condition in others, so repair is advised.

The oil tank base is defective in places and in poor condition elsewhere. Because the tank holds fuel, prompt repair by a competent contractor is advised, and the tank should be checked for leaks.

The site notes contain conflicting observations for the same elements, so please confirm the final condition of the garage roof, garage walls and oil tank base before this section is issued.

**Drainage**

The drainage system was inspected from ground level and, where access allowed, at the inspection chambers and gullies. Stored items limited access to some chambers and the gully at the back door, so parts of the system could not be fully examined.

The gully at the back door is partly blocked. It should be cleared and checked, and a drain specialist should confirm that water flows freely. Blockages at this point can lead to water pooling against the house. The gully is also recorded as defective or in poor condition in places, so repair is advised.

The soil and vent pipe is defective in places and in poor condition in others. Prompt repair by a competent contractor is advised, as faults in this pipe can allow foul odours into the house and may cause water to enter the walls.

The shared drain is defective in places and in poor condition elsewhere, with crack widths under 3 mm noted. Because it may serve neighbouring properties, the position on shared responsibility should be confirmed with the neighbours or the title deeds before repairs are agreed.

Gutters and rainwater pipes are in mixed condition. Several sections are defective or in poor condition, and repair is advised to prevent water overflowing onto walls, which may be linked to the damp readings noted elsewhere.

Surface water run-off is defective in places. Prompt repair is advised.

The site notes contain conflicting observations for the same elements, so please confirm the final condition of the shared drain and the gully at the back door before this section is issued.

**Insulation and energy**

The insulation and energy elements were assessed visually and, where access allowed, in the loft. Stored items limited access to parts of the loft and some areas of the house, so not all insulation could be inspected.

The loft insulation is currently 100 mm thick. The current recommendation is 270 mm, so topping up the insulation would improve the home's thermal performance. The loft insulation is also recorded as defective in places, and prompt repair by a competent contractor is advised.

The cavity wall fill is recorded as defective in places and in poor condition in others. A cavity wall specialist should check the fill, as poor performance can contribute to damp and heat loss.

The boiler is [withheld] years old. Its efficiency is recorded as defective or in poor condition in places, so servicing and a full efficiency check by a qualified heating engineer are advised. No gas safety record was seen, so a current Gas Safe certificate should be requested.

Draught stripping and the hot water cylinder insulation are in mixed condition. Several sections are defective or in poor condition, and improvements here would help reduce heat loss at low cost.

The window glazing is in mixed condition, with some sections defective and others in poor condition. Repair or replacement of the defective units is advised, and this should be considered alongside the decayed rear kitchen window frame noted earlier.

The energy performance certificate rating is recorded as poor in places. Improvements to loft insulation, cavity fill, glazing and the boiler would be the most effective ways to improve it.

The site notes contain conflicting observations for the same elements, so please confirm the final condition of the loft insulation and cavity fill before this section is issued.

I can't draft this section as the notes stand, for two reasons.

**1. The recent sales figures must be removed.** The notes include sale prices for similar houses on Kirkgate (£238,000 in March 2026 and £251,500 in June 2026). The instruction letter prohibits any market value or valuation figure in the report, and valuations are issued separately by a registered valuer. Quoting comparable sale prices would breach that constraint, so I have left them out. Please also note that these figures should not be used to comment on the asking price or whether the Lennoxes should buy, which is also outside the scope of this report.

**2. The site notes are not a reliable basis for this section.** Most entries for "location and local market" describe repairs to the street, parking, flood map, mining records, conservation status and local amenities. These are not physical elements of the property, so the defect-style wording ("prompt repair advised", "crack width under 1 mm") does not make sense for them. The entries also conflict with one another, with the same item recorded as both defective and in good condition.

**Suggested location section, drafted without the prohibited material:**

14 Kirkgate is a 1930s semi-detached house in Dunmore, a residential street. The property is close to local amenities, and the surrounding street and parking are in mixed condition. Some areas were limited by stored items, so these observations should be treated as provisional.

Matters to be checked before the report is issued:
- The flood map, mining records and conservation status for the address should be confirmed with official sources (for example, the Environment Agency flood maps, the Coal Authority search and the local planning authority). These are not for the surveyor to assess visually.
- Any conservation area designation may affect future alterations, so the Lennoxes should be told of it if it applies.
- The street and parking condition notes are inconsistent and should be verified on a further visit or confirmed with the client's solicitor.

If you can confirm the location searches and the final street and parking observations, I can revise this section to about 150 words.

**Summary for Mr and Mrs Lennox**

This report describes the condition of 14 Kirkgate, Dunmore, a 1930s three-bedroom semi-detached house with rendered cavity walls, a slate roof and a rear dormer. It was inspected on 7 October 2026. It is a condition report only. It does not include a valuation or a view on the asking price, and it does not advise whether you should buy the property.

**Overall condition.** The house is of sound construction in most respects. Parts of it need attention, and some of those parts need attention soon.

**What needs doing first.**
- **Damp and moisture.** Readings of 18 to 22 per cent were taken at the gable wall at skirting level, and the bathroom ceiling is stained beneath the dormer. Find and fix the source before any other cosmetic work.
- **Roof and dormer.** Two slates have slipped over the rear dormer. Repair them promptly to prevent further water entry.
- **Services.** The boiler is 14 years old, and no gas safety record was seen. Ask the seller for a current Gas Safe certificate and have the boiler serviced.
- **Drainage.** The gully at the back door is partly blocked, and the soil pipe and shared drain are defective in places. Clear and repair them promptly.
- **Garage roof.** It may contain asbestos. Do not disturb it, and have it tested before any work.

**Other repairs, within the next year.** Flaunching to the chimney is cracked. The rear kitchen window cill is decayed. Loft insulation is 100 mm and should be topped up to [withheld] mm. Cavity fill, the stair balustrade, the rear fence, the paths and patio, and several outbuildings need repair or replacement.

**Where the house stands overall.** The house has a number of defects, some urgent and some planned. The front wall and the hairline cracks to the front roughcast are not progressive, and the roof structure is sound. The most significant items are damp, the boiler and gas safety record, the drainage, and the outstanding repairs. Costs for these should be obtained from contractors before you proceed.

Some site observations conflict and should be confirmed before this report is final. Please read the full sections for detail.
